_about: Which spec files each Playwright project runs, read by playwright.config.ts and by scripts/e2e-shard.mjs, which deals the work of the chromium, roads, perf and evidence projects out to CI runners. `walkthrough` is a pattern of file names; the rest are lists of them. The chromium project runs every other spec file. `seconds` is how long each file of the chromium, perf and evidence projects takes on a CI runner with one worker, first attempts only. `testSeconds` is the same for each test of the roads project, which is dealt out test by test, named by its file and titles as Playwright's --test-list reads them. Do not edit either by hand: the weekly e2e timings run (.github/workflows/e2e-timings.yml, scripts/e2e-timings.mjs) takes them from the e2e-times.json files the CI jobs upload, and opens a pull request; `_timings` says which runs they came from (issue #229). A new spec file or roads test with no figure fails CI with a message that says what to add. The figures before the first weekly run came from single CI runs, by hand, from 16 to 19 November 2026, and the roads tests, frontage-ends.spec.ts, homes.spec.ts and undo-built-ground.spec.ts, which had none, from run 44562541789 (19 November 2026). guides.spec.ts, two-tabs.spec.ts and construction.spec.ts are estimates since issue #226 turned on cheap frames: their seconds before it times the ratio of their seconds after to before in the development container (4-core Xeon at 2.1 GHz, one worker, 19 November 2026, on main at d891dcd), 25/52, 24/47 and 19/36. The other files got cheaper too and keep their figures until the weekly run replaces them. `perf` and `evidence` are the files of those projects (issue #225): they run nightly, after each push to main and on pull requests that touch the renderer or carry the `perf` or `evidence` label, and they do not gate a merge (.github/workflows/perf.yml).

globalTimeout._about: Each CI runner's Playwright run stops at timesPlan times its planned minutes, and at no less than minMinutes, with --global-timeout from scripts/e2e-shard.mjs (issue #228). Playwright then fails the run and writes its report, where GitHub's job limit would stop the job with no report. A runner's plan is the sum of its files' seconds, or for a runner without files the plan its matrix entry gives. In the 156 chromium runners of the last 25 CI runs, first attempts took 1.33 times their files' seconds at the median, 2.17 at the 90th percentile and 2.68 at the 95th, and 1.6 at the median on an EPYC 7763. At 1.5 times, as the issue first asked, about four runners in ten that passed would have been stopped. minMinutes covers starting the servers and the production build. A runner also never gets less than its plan plus every attempt of its longest test (scripts/e2e-limits.mjs), so a test that times out still gets its retry.
